one_liner: Action officer at HQ Marine Corps (Quantico) managing taskers, correspondence, briefings, records compliance and POM/planning analysis for the Marine and Family Programs Division.
fit_summary: Daniel's government-client consulting at IEM, policy knowledge and people skills map well to tasker coordination, briefings and stakeholder communication. However, the posting asks for five years of experience plus comprehensive knowledge of Marine Corps structure, the Marine Corps Planning Process, POM and naval correspondence standards, and nothing on file shows military or DoD background. Those are the gaps Daniel would need to close.
eligibility: Open to the public; this is a nonappropriated fund (NAF) MCCS position, not competitive-service, so no federal status or veterans' preference is needed.
Five years of experience in the occupation is required; relevant education may substitute. Confirm Daniel's total years and degree.
No security clearance is required, but expect a background check typical of DoD installation jobs.
On-site at Quantico with no telework. Occasional travel and lifting up to 20 lbs.
strategy: Frame your IEM work as action-officer-style support to government clients: tracking deliverables and deadlines, coordinating across agencies, drafting reports and briefings for officials. Describe only duties you actually did.
State dates, hours per week and total years plainly, and show that your experience adds up to five years. Cite education if it helps substitute for experience.
Emphasize writing and briefing senior officials, records and data handling, and program assessment. Mirror the posting's terms, such as taskers, point papers and coordination.
Address the Marine Corps gap honestly. Note any DoD or military-family client work, and study MCPP, the POM cycle and SECNAV M-5216.5 (naval correspondence) before interviews.
Keep the resume to two pages even though this is a NAF job, and apply before November 12, 2026. Quantico is a short commute from Manassas, which is worth noting as a local candidate.
resume_bullets: Coordinated [number] client deliverables/tasks for [federal/state/local agency] emergency management programs, tracking deadlines and follow-up to ensure [on-time/accurate] responses.
Drafted [reports/briefings/point papers] for [senior officials/agency leadership] on [disaster recovery/preparedness topic], synthesizing input from [number] subject matter experts.
Analyzed [program/plan/data] against [guidance/model], identifying [resource or compliance issues] and recommending [action].
interview_questions: Describe how you would track and route multiple short-suspense taskers across several branches at once.
Tell us about a time you briefed a senior official. How did you prepare, and how did you handle tough questions?
What do you know about the Marine Corps POM process or the Marine and Family Programs Division?
How would you get timely, accurate input from program staff who are slow to respond?
watch_outs: The Marine Corps-specific knowledge requirements (MCPP, POM, naval correspondence) may favor veterans or prior HQMC staff.
NAF positions offer different benefits and pay rules than GS jobs, and promotion potential is listed as NA.
The application window is short (October 29 to November 12, 2026), and the job is fully on-site with no telework.
